lessons: Reviewer assertions must be verified, not transcribed. The expert audit asserted the kupot group LTC policy was ordered wound up from 1.7.2025 / 1.1.2026. That was a Ministry of Health DRAFT that never issued and was dropped; the June 2026 Comptroller report treats the arrangement as live. The irreversibility argument stands instead on the sourced fact that individual policies are no longer sold at all.

The same audit asserted that waiving שאירים cover is pure waste for a member with no survivors. Verification INVERTED it: re-adding the cover permits medical underwriting and the fund may exclude a pre-existing condition, so it is a one-way door unless ביטוח המשך is kept. The skill now raises the waiver WITH the trap.

A v1.0.0 claim that group policies were 'never auto-converted' by the שקל ראשון reform could not be sourced and is probably wrong; the sourced position is that the group market was affected far less and with delay. Corrected in both languages and added to the do-not-assert list. This had defined the skill's stated core audience for a full version.

'עיסוק סביר' is commentary shorthand, not the takanon's term; the string does not appear in the takanon at all. The skill now quotes the actual definition (25% capacity, 90 consecutive days) and labels the shorthand as shorthand.

verify-evidence.py --check-sources has a false-negative mode: an unbalanced '<' anywhere on a page makes the <[^>]+> stripper delete everything to the next '>'. On the National Health Insurance Law that removed 78,282 characters including the children's dental item, so a correct verbatim snippet failed. Flagged to the admin; NOT patched, because the file had uncommitted changes.

The evidence extractor matches percentages, NIS amounts and URLs, so it never flagged circular numbers, statutory section numbers or Hebrew verbatim quotes. Eleven such claims had been unjustified since v1.0.0 and were only caught by the Judge. Worth extending the extractor.

lessons: The direct read changed the wording, not the thesis. The 1.4.0 claim (the health area shows the kupa's cover and flags duplicates) held; the secondary-source detail around it (tag names, colours) did not. Rule: quote a tool's own pages for its vocabulary, and when only guides are available say 'per guides' in the skill text itself, as 1.4.0 did, so the correction is a swap and not a retraction.

Public FAQ pages of a logged-in government application are a primary source for how the application describes itself and are readable without identification. The login landing page (login.gov.il: ID + password + SMS, biometric ID or smart card) is where the skill must stop; the personal screens ('תמונת מצב') remain unread and the skill says so.

The regulator's consumer FAQ can lag its own circulars: it still states the generic 50%-of-ADL trigger and does not mention the 1.1.2025 group amendment. A primary source is not automatically the current rule; the policy wording wins, and the skill now says which source to quote for which fact.

The 60-day regret window after cancelling a private health policy is the first genuinely reversible cut found in this domain. It belongs in Step H and in the cancellation letter (date the notice), scoped to private health policies only until an insurer confirms it for another branch.

The 'health area shows the policyholder only' fact closes a trap the skill itself set in 1.4.0: Step A sent users to it right after the per-adult rule, which invited reading children's covers off it. A new data source has to be checked for scope (who, what period, what is excluded) before it is wired into a step.

Harmonising HE to EN by rewriting HE as a mirror of the final EN, rather than trimming the old HE sentence by sentence, was faster and safer: 23 headers aligned by construction, and every removed paragraph had a named destination in a -he reference before it was removed. Hebrew came out ~15% shorter than the English for the same content, which is the usual ratio and leaves headroom under the cap.
